meta.storyTitle: Run and report a security-only review

summary.prose: This Story adds the module that actually runs a dedicated security review: it dispatches the code-vulnerability pass through the CLI model s1 selected, folds in the dependency advisories s2 already collected, drives the review through two rounds using the review framework's existing shared machinery, and assembles one report that clearly separates confirmed findings from gaps it could not verify. Nothing in this report is a new data shape -- it is built entirely out of the already-typed SecurityFinding and VerificationReceipt records.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic adds a standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/) that owns model selection, dependency-advisory collection, code-assessment execution, and reporting, and supplies review-round's existing RoundDriverHooks.security hook as a thin adapter. review-round itself stays unchanged except for the one call site invoking that hook; the data shapes it already exports (SecurityFinding, SecurityLocator, EvidenceProvider, VerificationReceipt) are populated, never redefined.

ownedContracts.name: SecurityReviewEntryPoint
ownedContracts.purpose: The daemon IPC method + MCP tool (insrc_security_review_step) a caller actually invokes to trigger a security review -- mirroring insrc_code_review_step's phase-driven shape and its confirm_wait-on-stale-index pattern, collapsed to a single always-daemon-reviews path since the pinned security model always performs the actual assessment, never the controller.

consumedContracts.name: SecurityModelSelection
consumedContracts.purpose: Carries s1's resolved security-model identity (or its unavailability) across the boundary so s3 can dispatch the code-vulnerability pass through CliProvider.runReadOnlySession with that exact model, record the effective model in the report without re-resolving it, and refuse with the blocker reason rather than falling back silently.

consumedContracts.name: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
consumedContracts.purpose: Carries s2's dependency-advisory collection outcome across the boundary: the pinned contentIdentity it was collected against, the queried coordinates, the actual advisory matches, the per-match advisory destination recorded for audit, the per-manager input mode used, and the dependencies/sources that stayed unresolved or unavailable. contentStable records whether s2's own post-audit re-verification matched its pre-audit value; each perManagerMode[] entry carries configuredDestination (a configured value, never claimed as independently observed).

boundary.internal: The RoundDriverHooks.security adapter function; the CliProvider.runReadOnlySession dispatch of the code-vulnerability pass against the SAME pinned contentIdentity s2 collected against (recomputed/verified by s3, refusing on a content MISMATCH only), using s1's resolved model, with the SAME host access every other CLI-backed session in this codebase already has. The call into runReviewRound and the separate ownership of everything runReviewRound itself does NOT do (round reconciliation, VerificationReceipt persistence, checkpoint cleanup); the mapping from contentIdentity onto the epicHash/storyId identity persistVerificationReceipt requires; and the assembly of SecurityFinding/SecurityEvidence plus a supplemental report structure stay private to s3.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Model-tier resolution, availability/credential checks, and no-silent-fallback blocker-reporting stay private to s1; only SecurityModelSelection crosses its boundary.

pkg_audit's package-manager resolution, controller-equivalent-access dependency collection, contentIdentity computation and per-manager destination recording stay private to s2; only SecurityAdvisoryEvidence crosses its boundary.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B -- run and report the security-only review

nonFunctional.security: s3's code-vulnerability pass is dispatched through CliProvider.runReadOnlySession with the same access level every other CLI-backed session in this codebase already has; no additional credential/out-of-scope/MCP denial or negative-access test gates dispatch (k2). contentIdentity remains a hard CORRECTNESS invariant: s3 recomputes and verifies it before trusting s2's evidence, refusing ONLY on an actual content mismatch or contentStable:false.
nonFunctional.observability: Every checkpointed round is recorded as a VerificationReceipt (receipt-record.ts); s3 owns stamping it with the epicHash/storyId persistVerificationReceipt requires, deterministically derived from the review's own pinned contentIdentity.
nonFunctional.durability: No new persistent storage is introduced; the durable records are the already-typed SecurityFinding/VerificationReceipt heads the shared round-driver machinery persists, plus s3's SecurityReviewReport, which stays in-memory only and is never a stored artifact type.
nonFunctional.performance: Bounded by one CLI read-only session per request per round, not a background job.

api.name: runSecurityReview
api.signature: function runSecurityReview(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets, opts: { readonly reviewId: string; readonly modelSelection: SecurityModelSelection; readonly advisoryEvidence: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence; readonly now: string; readonly epicHash?: string; readonly storyId?: string }): Promise<SecurityReviewReport>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The registered repo root every targets.entries path is validated against.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The review's content scope; recomputed against to verify s2's pinned contentIdentity.

parameters.name: opts
parameters.type: { reviewId, modelSelection, advisoryEvidence, now, epicHash?, storyId? }
parameters.purpose: The review's identity plus s1's and s2's already-resolved outputs. epicHash/storyId are OPTIONAL: supplied (reviewing inside an existing tracked Epic/Story) -> threaded directly into persistVerificationReceipt's ident with standalone left unset; omitted -> derived via deriveReceiptIdentity with standalone:true.

errors.condition: Recomputed contentIdentity does not match advisoryEvidence.contentIdentity, or contentStable is false.

preconditions: modelSelection and advisoryEvidence are already resolved by s1/s2.
targets.entries paths all resolve inside repoPath (validated before any I/O).
postconditions: The ENTIRE body (both rounds, reconciliation, every writeCheckpoint/renderReviewReport/finalizeAndCleanup call, and both persistVerificationReceipt calls) runs inside runInStepContext({cwd: repoPath, envRepo: repoPath}, ...) (src/shared/step-context.ts) -- the production mechanism, not a test-only seam, that binds checkpoint.ts/reconciliation.ts/review-report.ts's own ambient resolveRepoPath(undefined) calls to THIS repoPath, never the caller's own ambient session repo.

contentIdentity is reverified (verifyContentIdentityMatch) a SECOND time immediately before round 2 dispatches and a THIRD time immediately before persisting round 2's receipt/report; any divergence detected at either point aborts the review with ContentIdentityMismatchError, distinct from s2's own contentStable (which covers only s2's OWN collection window, not s3's).

ONE VerificationReceipt is persisted PER ROUND (matching the HLD's own 'every checkpointed round is recorded as a VerificationReceipt'): round 1's and round 2's receipt.id are distinct ({reviewId}-round-1 / {reviewId}-round-2); a round that throws (timeout, identity divergence after it started) still persists a result:'fail' receipt for THAT round before the error propagates -- never silently skipped. A refusal BEFORE any round starts (contentIdentity mismatch at entry, modelSelection unavailable) persists nothing, since no execution occurred yet.
Round-1 code findings and s2's dependency-advisory findings carry round 1's receipt.id; round-2 code findings carry round 2's receipt.id.
On success a final VerificationReceipt pass/fail pair exists and the scratch folder is cleaned up via finalizeAndCleanup; on a pre-flight refusal, neither a receipt nor a checkpoint exists.

api.name: buildSecurityRoundHooks
api.signature: function buildSecurityRoundHooks(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets, modelSelection: SecurityModelSelection, reviewId: string): RoundDriverHooks<SecurityFinding>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Threaded into the security hook for path validation.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: Closed over by the returned hooks.

parameters.name: modelSelection
parameters.purpose: The pinned model identity.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.purpose: Logging context only.

returns.meaning: {reviewKind:'code', checkpointGranularity:'round', ground: async()=>[], security: runSecurityCodePass bound to these args}.

api.name: runSecurityCodePass
api.signature: function runSecurityCodePass(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets, modelSelection: SecurityModelSelection, round: number): Promise<readonly SecurityFinding[]>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The cwd for ReadOnlySessionOpts.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: Scopes the prompt.

parameters.name: modelSelection
parameters.purpose: Supplies the pinned modelId.

parameters.name: round
parameters.purpose: 1 initial, 2 correction-and-re-review.

returns.meaning: Structured findings from the CLI session's schema-validated output.

api.name: verifyContentIdentityMatch
api.signature: function verifyContentIdentityMatch(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets, advisoryEvidence: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence): Promise<void>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Passed through to computeContentIdentity.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The SAME targets s2 was given.

parameters.name: advisoryEvidence
parameters.purpose: Carries the pinned contentIdentity and contentStable flag.

api.name: deriveReceiptIdentity
api.signature: function deriveReceiptIdentity(contentIdentity: string): { readonly epicHash: string; readonly storyId: string }

parameters.name: contentIdentity
parameters.purpose: The review's pinned content identity.

returns.meaning: epicHash = createHash('sha256').update('security-review:'+contentIdentity).digest('hex').slice(0,16) -- exactly 16 lowercase hex characters, matching this codebase's own artifactJsonPath-enforced id convention (src/workflow/tracker/resolve.ts's LLD_RE/STORY_RE: /^...-([0-9a-f]{16})-(s\d+)\.../); storyId = the fixed literal 's1' (matches the SAME regex's (s\d+) group and admission.ts's /^s\d+$/ check -- 's-security' does NOT match and was rejected by both probes this round).

postconditions: Pure and synchronous; no new persistent mapping table.

Tested through the REAL receipt persistence/read-back path (persistVerificationReceipt + readReceiptRecord), not just as a string-shape unit test, so an id the storage layer itself rejects is caught here rather than first in production.

api.name: assembleSecurityReport
api.signature: function assembleSecurityReport(advisoryEvidence: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence, codeFindings: readonly SecurityFinding[], reconciliation: readonly ReconciliationResult[], receipts: { readonly round1: VerificationReceipt; readonly round2: VerificationReceipt }, modelSelection: SecurityModelSelection, baseReport: { readonly path: string; readonly markdown: string }): SecurityReviewReport

parameters.name: advisoryEvidence
parameters.purpose: Supplies confirmed matches plus unresolved/unavailable gaps.

parameters.name: codeFindings
parameters.purpose: Round 2's own output.

parameters.name: reconciliation
parameters.purpose: Attached for audit only.

parameters.name: receipts
parameters.purpose: Both rounds' persisted receipts; round 1's id is stamped onto dependency-advisory findings and round 1's code findings, round 2's id onto round 2's code findings.

parameters.name: modelSelection
parameters.purpose: FR001's 'record the effective model in the report' -- carried into SecurityReviewReport.effectiveModel and into supplementalMarkdown, never re-resolved.

parameters.name: baseReport
parameters.purpose: renderReviewReport's own unmodified output.

returns.meaning: {findings, unresolvedDependencies, unavailableSources, reconciliation, receipts, effectiveModel: {provider, modelId}, baseReportMarkdown, supplementalMarkdown} -- never persisted as its own artifact.

preconditions: Called once, after both rounds and the receipt exist.
postconditions: Dependency-advisory findings and round-1 code findings carry receiptId:receipts.round1.id; round-2 code findings carry receiptId:receipts.round2.id.

effectiveModel is copied from modelSelection as-dispatched (status:'configured' always, by this point) -- never re-derived from config, so the report always names the model that ACTUALLY ran, not whatever is currently configured.

api.name: handleSecurityReviewStep

parameters.name: request
parameters.purpose: A fresh phase:'start' request (repo/targets/epicHash?/storyId?) or a resumption after confirm_wait ({phase:'start', state, proceed}).

returns.meaning: {next:'confirm_wait', state, guidance} when the repo's graph index is stale relative to the pinned content (the security model's own insrc_analyze/insrc_analyze_step drill-down tool calls would otherwise read stale data) and the caller has not yet said proceed; otherwise {next:'done', report, markdown} after running the whole review end-to-end: resolveSecurityModel (s1), collectDependencyAdvisories (s2), then runSecurityReview (s3's own orchestrator).

preconditions: This is the ONLY function the daemon IPC handler and the insrc_security_review_step MCP tool call -- neither registers its own orchestration logic.
postconditions: A resume call (state + proceed:false) runs the review against the index as-is, the same as code-review's degraded/diff-based review path, never silently waiting again.
A resume call (state + proceed:true) waits for the index to catch up (bounded) before running the review.
epicHash/storyId on the ORIGINAL request, if supplied, are passed straight through into runSecurityReview's opts unchanged; handleSecurityReviewStep itself never re-derives or second-guesses them.

The repo-binding fix (runInStepContext) and the per-round receipt/content-identity logic live inside runSecurityReview, not duplicated here -- handleSecurityReviewStep is a thin phase/resume wrapper only.

dataModelChanges.details: The Story's own in-memory return shape, never persisted as a tracked artifact (resolved open question qfab24fea). {findings, unresolvedDependencies, unavailableSources, reconciliation, receipts: {round1, round2}, effectiveModel: {provider, modelId}, baseReportMarkdown, supplementalMarkdown}. receipts is now a PAIR (one per round, matching the HLD's 'every checkpointed round is recorded as a VerificationReceipt'), not a single shared receipt. effectiveModel carries FR001's 'record the effective model in the report' requirement, copied from the modelSelection actually dispatched, never re-resolved.
Thrown by verifyContentIdentityMatch on a recomputed-identity mismatch or advisoryEvidence.contentStable===false.

The daemon IPC method's and insrc_security_review_step MCP tool's own request/response shapes (sc3's interfaceSketch). A fresh request carries repo/targets/epicHash?/storyId?; a resumption after confirm_wait carries state+proceed. The response is either confirm_wait (with a state token to resume) or done (with the SecurityReviewReport and its rendered markdown).

interactionWithShared.howDetails: runSecurityReview reads modelSelection as-is, refusing with blockerReason on 'unavailable', otherwise threading modelId into buildSecurityRoundHooks -> runSecurityCodePass.
verifyContentIdentityMatch recomputes identity against advisoryEvidence; assembleSecurityReport maps matches/unresolvedDependencies/unavailableSources through unchanged.

handleSecurityReviewStep IS sc3: it is the daemon IPC method + MCP tool body. On a fresh request it checks the repo's index freshness via resolveRepoLastIndexedAt(repoPath) against the request's targets; if stale, it returns confirm_wait with a state token rather than silently running the model's drill-down tools against outdated graph data. Otherwise -- or on a resumed proceed:true/false call -- it resolves sc1 (resolveSecurityModel) and sc2 (collectDependencyAdvisories) itself, then calls runSecurityReview and returns done.

errorCases.scenario: Recomputed contentIdentity over targets does not match advisoryEvidence.contentIdentity.
errorCases.detection: verifyContentIdentityMatch compares the two strings byte-for-byte before any round runs.
errorCases.response: Throw ContentIdentityMismatchError(expected, actual, contentStable); no round dispatches, no receipt persisted.
errorCases.userImpact: The review is refused outright; the caller must re-run s2's collection against current content.

errorCases.detection: verifyContentIdentityMatch checks this flag even when identity strings match.
errorCases.response: Throw ContentIdentityMismatchError with contentStable:false; same refusal path.
errorCases.userImpact: The review is refused; the caller re-runs s2's collection for a stable read.

errorCases.detection: runSecurityReview checks status before constructing any hooks.
errorCases.response: Throw SecurityModelUnavailableError(blockerReason); no fallback model is attempted.
errorCases.userImpact: The review reports the exact blocker instead of silently using a different model.

errorCases.scenario: runSecurityCodePass's CliProvider.runReadOnlySession call exceeds its deadline.
errorCases.detection: ReadOnlySessionTimeoutError thrown by runReadOnlySession itself, never internally retried.
errorCases.response: Propagated out of runSecurityCodePass -> hooks.security -> runReviewRound, but FIRST caught by runSecurityReview's own per-round try/catch: a result:'fail' VerificationReceipt is persisted for THAT round (round1 or round2, whichever was executing) before the error is rethrown. No automatic resumption is attempted: round-1 findings are never durably cached anywhere resumable (writeCheckpoint stores only {reviewId, lastCompletedUnit}, not the findings themselves), so a retry of the WHOLE runSecurityReview call restarts cleanly at round 1 -- this is a deliberate restart-always design, not an unintended gap: readCheckpoint is read only for observability (surfacing that a prior attempt existed), never to skip a round.
errorCases.userImpact: The review fails for that round, but the failure itself is now durably recorded (a 'fail' receipt), not silently lost; a retry always restarts at round 1, deterministically, rather than attempting a partial resume the design cannot actually support.

errorCases.detection: finalizeAndCleanup's own documented contract leaves the scratch folder intact on a durable-copy failure.
errorCases.response: Propagated unchanged; the already-persisted VerificationReceipt is not rolled back.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller sees the persistence failure, but the receipt and round outputs are not lost.

errorCases.scenario: reconcileRound returns a verdicts array whose length does not match priorFindings.length.
errorCases.detection: reconcileRound's own internal check throws before returning.
errorCases.response: Propagated unchanged; s3 does not paper over a reconciliation-module internal-contract violation.
errorCases.userImpact: The review fails with the reconciliation module's own error.

errorCases.scenario: targets.entries contains a path outside repoPath.
errorCases.detection: s3's own path-containment check, run before any I/O.
errorCases.response: Throw synchronously before computeContentIdentity or any CLI dispatch.
errorCases.userImpact: The review is refused immediately with a clear out-of-scope-path message.

errorCases.scenario: The repo's graph index is stale relative to the pinned content when handleSecurityReviewStep's first phase:'start' call is made.
errorCases.detection: resolveRepoLastIndexedAt(repoPath) returns a timestamp older than the content the request targets.
errorCases.response: Return {next:'confirm_wait', state, guidance} instead of running any round; the caller must re-call with {phase:'start', state, proceed} to continue.
errorCases.userImpact: The controller is asked whether to wait for a fresh index (more accurate drill-down) or proceed anyway (degraded, since the model's own insrc_analyze/insrc_analyze_step tool calls would read stale data) -- never silently one or the other.

errorCases.scenario: contentIdentity, reverified immediately before round 2 or before persisting round 2's receipt/report, no longer matches the value verified before round 1 (a persistent edit during round 1 or between rounds).
errorCases.detection: verifyContentIdentityMatch is called a second and third time (not just once before round 1); a mismatch at either point is detected the same way as the original pre-flight check.
errorCases.response: Throw ContentIdentityMismatchError; a result:'fail' VerificationReceipt is persisted for the round that was executing when the divergence was caught, then the error propagates -- the review never finalizes a report against content different from what round 1 (and s2's advisories) actually reviewed.
errorCases.userImpact: A review is aborted mid-run rather than silently producing a report whose findings describe two different trees; the caller must restart once the repository is back to a stable state.

errorCases.scenario: The caller's own session repo (whatever resolveRepoPath(undefined) would resolve to) differs from the explicit repoPath this review targets.
errorCases.detection: Without binding, checkpoint.ts/reconciliation.ts/review-report.ts's own ambient resolveRepoPath(undefined) calls would silently resolve to the CALLER's repo, not repoPath.
errorCases.response: runSecurityReview wraps its entire body in runInStepContext({cwd: repoPath, envRepo: repoPath}, ...) (src/shared/step-context.ts) so every nested helper call binds to the SAME explicit repoPath, never the ambient session repo.
errorCases.userImpact: A caller working in repo A can request (and get) a review correctly scoped to a different repo B -- findings, checkpoints, reports and receipts never split across repositories.

edgeCases.input: The code pass finds zero findings and advisoryEvidence.matches is also empty.
edgeCases.expected: SecurityReviewReport.findings is empty; a VerificationReceipt with result:'pass' is still persisted.

edgeCases.input: advisoryEvidence.matches is non-empty but unresolvedDependencies is also non-empty.
edgeCases.expected: Both reported distinctly: confirmed matches become findings, unresolvedDependencies carried through verbatim, never merged.

edgeCases.input: Round 2 finds zero findings where round 1 found some.
edgeCases.expected: reconcileRound classifies round 1's findings 'no-longer-surfaced'; findings reflect round 2's own result.
computeContentIdentity still produces a stable identity; the code pass is expected to return zero findings -- a well-defined degenerate review, not an error.

edgeCases.input: A manager has mode:'unsupported' alongside others that succeeded.
edgeCases.expected: supplementalMarkdown surfaces the unsupported manager as an explicit coverage gap, distinct from successfully-audited managers' findings.

handleSecurityReviewStep runs the review against the index as-is; this is a DEGRADED run (equivalent to code-review's diff-only path), not an error -- the report is still fully populated, just potentially grounded on stale drill-down data for the model's own tool calls.

edgeCases.input: Two concurrent runSecurityReview calls target different repos (A and B) from sessions that otherwise share the same ambient cwd.
edgeCases.expected: Each call's own runInStepContext scope is independent (AsyncLocalStorage, not a global/process-wide override) -- A's helpers resolve to A, B's to B, even though both run concurrently in the same process.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The reviewer runs with the same host access as the controller itself -- no sandboxing, egress restriction, or filesystem confinement beyond CliProvider.runReadOnlySession's own tool allowlist.
Cloud inference for the security review's code pass uses the installed CLI provider, never a direct REST call.

testLevels.purpose: Exercise s3's own pure/deterministic logic without any real CLI session, filesystem, or network I/O.
subjects: deriveReceiptIdentity -- same contentIdentity always re-derives the identical pair; different identities derive different pairs.
verifyContentIdentityMatch -- resolves on a match with contentStable:true; throws on mismatch; throws on contentStable:false even when identity matches.

assembleSecurityReport -- confirmed matches map to dependency-advisory SecurityFindings with checkId:'dependency-advisory' and receiptId stamped; unresolvedDependencies/unavailableSources pass through verbatim; empty inputs produce an empty findings array.
buildSecurityRoundHooks -- hooks.ground always resolves to [] without I/O; hooks.security delegates to the injected code-pass function.

deriveReceiptIdentity's output is exercised through the REAL persistVerificationReceipt + readReceiptRecord round trip (not just asserted as a string shape) -- catches an id the storage layer itself would reject.

testLevels.purpose: Exercise runSecurityReview's full orchestration against the real review-round/ machinery, with only the CLI session faked via an injected test double.
subjects: runSecurityReview end-to-end: round 1, correction round 2, reconciliation, a real persisted+read-back VerificationReceipt, and real checkpoint cleanup.
runSecurityReview refuses before any round dispatches on a contentIdentity mismatch.
runSecurityReview refuses before any round dispatches on modelSelection.status:'unavailable', verified via the fake CLI session never being called.
A clean-run case still persists a VerificationReceipt with result:'pass'.

handleSecurityReviewStep: a stale-index fresh request returns confirm_wait with a state token, never runs a round; a resumed call with proceed:true or proceed:false both reach done; epicHash/storyId supplied on the request are threaded into the persisted receipt unchanged (standalone unset), while an omitted pair is derived via deriveReceiptIdentity with standalone:true.

runSecurityReview persists ONE VerificationReceipt per round (round1, round2), each with the correct result ('pass' on success, 'fail' on that round's own execution failure); a round-1 failure persists only round1's fail receipt and never dispatches round 2.

runSecurityReview reverifies contentIdentity before round 2 and before finalization; a repository edit injected between round 1 and round 2 in the test fixture is caught and aborts with ContentIdentityMismatchError, with round1's receipt already durably persisted as 'pass' from before the edit.

runSecurityReview run with repoPath=B while the test harness's own ambient cwd is A: writeCheckpoint/reconcileRound/renderReviewReport/finalizeAndCleanup all read/write under B, verified by asserting on B's own .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ contents, never A's -- proves the runInStepContext binding, not a global test override.

SecurityReviewReport.effectiveModel matches the modelSelection actually passed in, in a case where it differs from the repo's currently-configured tier default (proving the report never re-resolves configuration).

provingTests: unit: assembleSecurityReport separates confirmed matches from unresolved/unavailable gaps
integration: runSecurityReview end-to-end populates SecurityFinding/VerificationReceipt unchanged

integration: handleSecurityReviewStep end-to-end -- a fresh request with a fresh index reaches done directly; a stale index reaches confirm_wait first (proves ac3's 'when a user requests a security review' actually has a caller-invocable trigger).

integration: runSecurityReview persists a per-round VerificationReceipt pair with correctly-formatted (16-hex epicHash, s\d+ storyId) identity, readable back through readReceiptRecord, and the report carries effectiveModel -- closing all four HIGH + two MED findings from the revision-2 review.

alternativesConsidered.name: Security-hook adapter, no-op ground
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Supply hooks.security as the real CliProvider.runReadOnlySession adapter (matching the HLD's own literal framing) and hooks.ground as a trivial, zero-cost function that always resolves to [] -- runReviewRound's unconditional ground call costs nothing extra since it never performs I/O.
alternativesConsidered.approach: s3's new orchestrator module builds one RoundDriverHooks<SecurityFinding> object per review: ground=async()=>[] (a one-line, synchronous-resolving no-op -- a security-only review has no general code-quality ground pass to run, and review-round's own ground pass belongs to a sibling Story, out of scope here), security=the real adapter that resolves s1's SecurityModelSelection, builds the code-review prompt/schema, calls CliProvider.runReadOnlySession with s1's pinned modelId against repoPath/targets, and maps the structured result into SecurityFinding[] (plus s2's SecurityAdvisoryEvidence folded in as dependency-advisory SecurityFindings). The module calls runReviewRound(reviewId, hooks, round, targets) for round 1 and round 2 (correction-and-re-review), reconcileRound between them, writeCheckpoint after each, renderReviewReport for the base report, persistVerificationReceipt once at the end (ident derived from contentIdentity per q860d1b4e), finalizeAndCleanup last. This is the ONLY alternative whose wiring matches the HLD's own stated framework text verbatim ('supplies review-round's existing RoundDriverHooks.security hook as a thin adapter').
pros: Matches the HLD's own literal framework text (hooks.security, not hooks.ground) -- no silent deviation from the approved design
Reuses runReviewRound, reconcileRound, writeCheckpoint/readCheckpoint/finalizeAndCleanup, renderReviewReport, persistVerificationReceipt completely unchanged -- zero new code in review-round/ itself
The no-op ground costs nothing (no I/O, resolves immediately) so there is no real waste from the unconditional hooks.ground call
cons: Two hook fields (ground + security) for what is conceptually a single pass reads slightly oddly in isolation -- mitigated by a clear doc comment on the hooks object explaining why ground is a no-op for this review kind

alternativesConsidered.name: Real logic in ground, security left undefined
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Put the real CliProvider adapter in hooks.ground directly and leave hooks.security undefined, since ground always runs and the field names are otherwise interchangeable at the type level.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same orchestrator and same runReviewRound/reconcileRound/checkpoint/report/receipt calls as a1, but the roles of ground and security are swapped: hooks.ground is the real adapter, hooks.security is omitted (driver.ts's own code treats hooks.security as optional and skips calling it when undefined, exactly mirroring a1's no-op case from the other side).
pros: Saves writing the trivial no-op ground function -- one field, not two, carries the real work
Functionally identical findings output to a1 since runReviewRound only ever concatenates whatever both hooks return
cons: Contradicts the HLD's own explicit framework text, which names hooks.security (not hooks.ground) as the adapter s3 supplies -- a reviewer checking the implementation against the HLD would find a literal mismatch requiring either an HLD wording fix or a confusing explanation

Loses the self-documenting signal that this pass is specifically a SECURITY pass -- a future maintainer reading RoundDriverHooks usage elsewhere (the sibling general-review Story) would see 'ground' used for an ordinary code-quality pass there and a security pass here, with no field-name cue to tell them apart
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally equivalent to a1 but contradicts the HLD's literal hooks.security framing for no compensating benefit.

alternativesConsidered.name: Bypass runReviewRound with a dedicated security-review loop
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Write s3's own round-loop, reconciliation-call, and checkpoint-call sequencing directly, instead of going through the shared runReviewRound entry point.
alternativesConsidered.approach: s3 implements its own async function that performs the same sequence runReviewRound already performs (call the security logic for round N, concatenate results) but inline, without calling driver.ts's runReviewRound at all -- reasoning that a security-only review has no 'ground' concept and the two-hook abstraction is unnecessary overhead for a caller that only ever wants one kind of finding.
pros: Avoids ever constructing a hooks object with an empty/unused field
Slightly fewer lines in the immediate call site
cons: Duplicates runReviewRound's own round-validation logic (the RangeError on round<1, the synchronous-throw contract) -- a second, divergent implementation of the exact same round-driving rule this codebase already has once, in exactly the place the HLD says to reuse it ('S001... Initial Review and Correction-and-Re-review run through this exact same function')

Directly violates the HLD's own explicit text naming runReviewRound and RoundDriverHooks.security as what s3 drives -- this is an HLD back-flow-worthy deviation, not a Story-local implementation choice, and there is no finding motivating one

Breaks the sibling round-driver Story's own invariant that EVERY review (design or security) goes through the one shared driver -- a future change to round-driving behavior (e.g. a new checkpoint timing rule) would need to be duplicated into s3's private loop by hand
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Bypasses and duplicates the already-built, shared runReviewRound/RoundDriverHooks machinery the HLD explicitly says to reuse.

citations.ref: External reviewer finding (revision 2 review, 4 HIGH + 2 MED): invalid receipt identity format, checkpoint mistaken for verification execution, no mid-review content-identity revalidation, shared helpers resolving the wrong repository, checkpoint-recovery contradiction, missing effective-model in the report. All six confirmed against real code this round and fixed in revision 3.
